briefdescription.para: The check result, which formats the expressions.

detaileddescription.para: It formats its expression into the expression formatter, and retrieves the text when it reports the check.

briefdescription.para: The runner, which lists the test cases.

detaileddescription.para: It writes the list of the test cases with write_line().

briefdescription.para: The test case, which creates the checks.

detaileddescription.para: It passes the expression formatter to the check results created by expect() and require().

briefdescription.para: Size of the array that receives the elapsed time text.

detaileddescription.para: Large enough for ", time: 4294967295.999 ms", the longest text produced by format_elapsed_time().

briefdescription.para: Number of spaces per nesting level.

detaileddescription.para: Used by the concrete reporters to indent the lines of the nested test cases; four spaces is also the TAP 14 subtest indentation.

briefdescription.para: Size of the array that receives the totals text.

detaileddescription.para: Large enough for the longest text produced by format_session_totals(), which is longer than the texts of the suites and of the test cases: 53 characters, four counts, two fragments of up to 20 characters and a count each (the longest fragment is ", N test cases failed"), and the terminator, with the counts of the largest size_t value (10 digits on 32-bit targets, 20 on 64-bit ones). The fragments are counted at their maximum length, as the compiler does when it checks for truncation.
The array is a local variable of the functions that end the test cases, which run at the deepest point of the stack, so it is not larger than needed on the 32-bit embedded targets.

briefdescription.para: Whether to write an empty line before the next console output.

detaileddescription.para: Set and cleared by the concrete reporters, to separate the groups of console lines, such as the suites and the failed test cases; the output file is not affected.

briefdescription.para: The command-line arguments passed to the test runner.

detaileddescription.para: A view of the argv[] array of main(), copied from the session options by the constructor, and listed by write_info(), which is called only by begin_session(), within runner::initialise(); it is not used afterwards.

briefdescription.para: Output accumulation buffer.

detaileddescription.para: Accumulates all reporter output until it is written to the console or the output file via write_buffer_to_console() or write_buffer_to_file().

briefdescription.para: Whether the output buffer contains a failed check.

detaileddescription.para: Set by fail() and reset by clear_buffer(). When a nested test case begins, the concrete reporters use it to decide whether the results already buffered for the outer test case are displayed with normal verbosity.

briefdescription.para: ANSI colour codes for output formatting.

detaileddescription.para: Empty strings by default; the human reporter assigns detail::colours_red_green when colours are enabled by runner_options::colour, explicitly or because the console is a terminal.

briefdescription.para: Expression formatter for pass and fail reporting.

detaileddescription.para: Used by the checks (test_case::expect(), test_case::require(), and detail::check_result), which are friends, to pre-format expressions at construction time; pass() and fail() then append the formatted text to buffer_. The applications format their own types by defining operator<< for the public expression_formatter alias.

briefdescription.para: Whether the output file could not be opened.

detaileddescription.para: Set by the constructor, and returned by has_output_file_error().

briefdescription.para: Optional output file, receiving a copy of the test report.

detaileddescription.para: When non-null, the report is written to this file in addition to the console, without colour sequences. With the TAP reporter, the file receives the full report, regardless of the verbosity; with the human reporter, most of it only with the normal and verbose levels (see verbosity). The file is opened by the constructor and closed by the destructor.

briefdescription.para: Path of the optional output file.

detaileddescription.para: Copied by the constructor from the session options, so that the caller's string need not outlive runner::initialise(). Used to name the file in the confirmation message displayed when the file is closed (not displayed with the silent verbosity).

briefdescription.para: The verbosity level for test reporting.

detaileddescription.para: A copy of the level kept by the runner, set by the constructor from the same session options and not changed afterwards. The public accessor is runner::verbosity_level().

briefdescription.para: Constructor for the reporter class.

detaileddescription.para:
opts
The session options, passed to runner::initialise() or parsed by it from the command line.
Copies the verbosity and the view of the command-line arguments from the session options, and opens the output file, if a non-empty path was given, keeping a copy of the path. If the file cannot be opened, an error message is written to stderr, the report is written only to the console, and has_output_file_error() returns true. The internal string buffer is pre-allocated to reduce dynamic allocation overhead.

briefdescription.para: Virtual destructor for the reporter class.

detaileddescription.para: Virtual, so that the concrete reporters, owned through a pointer to this base class, are destroyed correctly.

If an output file was opened, it is flushed and closed, and a confirmation message naming the output file is written to stdout, except with the silent verbosity, which writes nothing to the console. If tracing is enabled, the function signature is output for diagnostic purposes.

briefdescription.para: Reports the abort of the test execution.

detaileddescription.para: Called by runner::abort() between begin_session() and end_session(), before the abort handler and ::abort(); neither the end_test_case() of the running test cases, if any, nor end_session() are called afterwards. The abort is caused either by a failed require(), when exceptions are disabled, after the failure was added to the output buffer, or by an explicit call of runner::abort(), from a test case body, from a suite body, or from the application.

Implementations display the buffered results, if any, with the context that identifies the running test case, followed by a line with the location of the abort, unless the verbosity is silent, and write them to the output file, if open, since the totals are never reached. They then clear the buffer, since the abort handler may throw an exception that the application catches, and the results must not be written again.

parameterdescription.para: The source location of the failed requirement, or of the runner::abort() call.
true if the abort is caused by a failed requirement.

briefdescription.para: Marks the beginning of a test session.

detaileddescription.para: Called by runner::initialise(), after the reporter is created; implementations display the session heading.

parameterdescription.para: Reference to the test runner.

briefdescription.para: Marks the beginning of a test suite.

detaileddescription.para: Called by suite::run() before the suite body, for the suites registered with runner::add_suite() and for the static suites, and by runner::initialise() for the top suite.

parameterdescription.para: Reference to the test suite.

briefdescription.para: Marks the beginning of a test case.

detaileddescription.para: Called by test_case::run() before the test case body; the results buffered for an outer test case, if any, are written first (see commit_outer_results()), so that the buffer is empty when the body starts.

parameterdescription.para: Reference to the test case.

briefdescription.para: Returns the comment-prefix string used by this reporter format.

detaileddescription.para: Used by write_info() to prefix the informational lines, so that they are valid comments in the output format.

briefdescription.para: Appends a line ending to the internal output buffer.

detaileddescription.para: Nothing is written to the console or to the output file; the buffer is written by the concrete reporters, at the end of each test case or suite.

Parameters
None.
Returns
Nothing.
This member function appends a newline character to the internal output buffer of the reporter. The buffer itself is written later, by the concrete reporters, at the end of each test case or suite, which then also flush the streams.

briefdescription.para: Marks the end of a test session.

detaileddescription.para: Called by runner::run(), after all suites have run; implementations display the session summary.

parameterdescription.para: Reference to the test runner.

briefdescription.para: Marks the end of a test suite.

detaileddescription.para: Called by suite::run() after the suite body, also when an exception escaped it, for the suites registered with runner::add_suite() and for the static suites, and by runner::run() for the top suite; implementations display the suite results.

parameterdescription.para: Reference to the test suite.

briefdescription.para: Marks the end of a test case.

detaileddescription.para: Called by test_case::run() after the test case body; implementations display the test case results and clear the output buffer.

parameterdescription.para: Reference to the test case.

briefdescription.para: Reports a failed condition.

detaileddescription.para:
failure
The failure details: the kind of the check, the message to display, whether the expression text is displayed, and the source location of the failure.
expression
The string representation of the expression.
test_case
The test case that owns this check.
Returns
Nothing.
Outputs a fail prefix (which includes the message and the source location), followed, when failure.has_expression is true, by the pre-formatted expression string, and a fail suffix.

briefdescription.para: Reports a failure of a test suite outside its test cases.

detaileddescription.para: Called by suite::run() when an exception escapes the suite body, between begin_suite() and end_suite(); the suite has already advanced to its next test point, which numbers the failure after the test cases already run. Implementations add a failed line to the output buffer, at the indentation of the test cases, which end_suite() displays; there is no source location to show.

parameterdescription.para: The message to display.
Reference to the test suite.

briefdescription.para: Flushes the standard output stream and the output file.

detaileddescription.para: Only the C streams are flushed; the internal output buffer is not written.

Parameters
None.
Returns
Nothing.
This member function flushes the stdout stream and, if open, the output file, so that everything already written to them becomes visible. It does not write the contents of the internal buffer.

briefdescription.para: Returns whether the output file could not be opened.

detaileddescription.para: Checked by runner::initialise(), which reports it as an option error; the report is then written only to the console.

Parameters
None.
true
The output file was requested but could not be opened.
false
No output file was requested, or it was opened.
Returns the flag set by the constructor when fopen() failed.

briefdescription.para: Output operator for boolean values.

detaileddescription.para:
v
The boolean value to output.
Reference to the current reporter instance.
This operator overload appends "true" or "false" to the internal output buffer of the reporter, as the expression formatter does. Being a non-template function, it is selected for bool values instead of the arithmetic template, which would format them as numbers.

briefdescription.para: Output operator for a single character.

detaileddescription.para:
c
The character to output.
Reference to the current reporter instance.
This operator overload appends the specified character to the internal output buffer of the reporter.

briefdescription.para: Output operator for a constant character string.

detaileddescription.para: Also selected for the non-const char pointers and arrays, which the pointer template does not accept. A null pointer is output as "nullptr".

s
The string to output, or a null pointer.
Reference to the current reporter instance.
This operator overload appends the contents of the provided C-style string to the internal output buffer of the reporter, or "nullptr" for a null pointer, as the expression formatter does; the char* values also reach this overload, and std::string::append() must not be called with a null pointer.

briefdescription.para: Output operator for the indentation manipulator.

detaileddescription.para: Appends indent_size_ spaces for each indentation level.

m
The indentation manipulator produced by indent(n).
Reference to the current reporter instance.
This operator overload appends spaces to the internal output buffer, indent_size_ for each of the m.level indentation levels, allowing *this << indent(n) << "text" chaining in both reporters.

briefdescription.para: Output operator for stream manipulators, such as endl.

detaileddescription.para:
func
Function pointer to the stream manipulator.
Reference to the current reporter instance.
This operator overload enables manipulators, such as endl, to be used with the reporter stream in a manner similar to standard C++ streams. When a manipulator function is passed, it is invoked with the current reporter instance.

briefdescription.para: Output operator for nullptr.

detaileddescription.para:
Reference to the current reporter instance.
This operator overload appends the string "nullptr" to the internal output buffer of the reporter, as the expression formatter does.

briefdescription.para: Output operator for std::string_view.

detaileddescription.para:
sv
The string view to output.
Reference to the current reporter instance.
This operator overload appends the contents of the provided std::string_view to the internal output buffer of the reporter.

briefdescription.para: Output operator to display any pointer.

detaileddescription.para: The char pointers are excluded, so that they are output as strings by the const char* overload, as the const char pointers are.

T
The type pointed to, other than char.
v
The pointer value to output.
Reference to the current reporter instance.
The address is formatted by the detail::append_pointer() helper, shared with the detail::expression_formatter, so that the pointers are displayed identically in the expressions and in the messages.

briefdescription.para: Output operator for arithmetic types.

detaileddescription.para:
T
The arithmetic type.
v
The value to output.
Reference to the current reporter instance.
This template operator overload allows the reporter to output values of any arithmetic type (integral or floating-point) in a consistent and readable format. The value is formatted using the detail::append_number() helper, without a type suffix (unlike the detail::expression_formatter operators, which add one).

briefdescription.para: Reports a passed condition.

detaileddescription.para:
message
The message to display.
expression
The string representation of the expression.
test_case
The test case that owns this check.
Returns
Nothing.
Outputs a pass prefix, followed by either the provided message or, if the message is empty, the evaluated expression string itself. A pass suffix is then appended to complete the output.

briefdescription.para: Reports a test suite skipped by the filter.

detaileddescription.para: Called by runner::run_suites(), instead of running the suite, when its name does not match the first filter pattern; the suite has already been assigned its index. Implementations display a single line, without the suite body.

parameterdescription.para: Reference to the skipped test suite.

briefdescription.para: Reports a test case skipped by the filter.

detaileddescription.para: Called instead of begin_test_case() and end_test_case(), when the name of the test case, or of its suite, does not match the filter pattern of its level; the test case has already been assigned its index. Implementations display a single line, at the indentation of the test case.

parameterdescription.para: Reference to the skipped test case.

briefdescription.para: Deprecated access to the verbosity level.

detaileddescription.para: Kept from the v5.0.1 reporter class, for the applications that read it through the deprecated runner::reporter() (tr.reporter ().verbosity ()). The level is the one returned by runner::verbosity_level(), from the same session options.

simplesect.para: The verbosity level of the session.

detaileddescription.para: Returns the level stored in verbosity_, set by the constructor.

briefdescription.para: Writes the current buffered content to the console.

detaileddescription.para: The console is the standard output stream; the buffer is written verbatim, without appending a line ending, and is not cleared.

Parameters
None.
Returns
Nothing.
This member function writes the contents of the internal output buffer to the console without appending a newline character. The buffer is not cleared; the caller is responsible for clearing it when appropriate.
The buffer is written with its size, not as a C string, so that a zero character in a message does not end the output.

briefdescription.para: Returns whether the passed checks are written anywhere.

detaileddescription.para: Called by test_case::expect() and test_case::require(), so that a passed check whose line is never written does not format its expression, its messages, or its line. The answer depends only on the verbosity and on the output file, which do not change during the session. A failed check is always formatted.

parameterdescription.para: The lines of the passed checks reach the console or the output file, at least in some cases.
The lines of the passed checks are never written.

briefdescription.para: Clears the output buffer.

detaileddescription.para: Also resets buffer_has_failures_, so that the flag always describes the current content of the buffer.

Parameters
None.
Returns
Nothing.
Empties buffer_, keeping its capacity, and resets buffer_has_failures_.

briefdescription.para: Writes the results buffered for the outer test case before a nested test case begins or is skipped.

detaileddescription.para: The concrete reporters decide where the results are written, and with which verbosity levels; the buffer is cleared.

briefdescription.para: Writes the results of the outer test case, if any, before a nested test case begins or is skipped.

detaileddescription.para: Called by begin_test_case() and skip_test_case() of the concrete reporters, so that the output follows the execution order.

Parameters
None.
Returns
Nothing.
For a nested test case, the outer test case may have performed checks before it; their results are written first, by commit_buffer(). For a top-level test case, the buffer is expected to be empty, since the checks are performed only by the test cases, and each one writes its results when it ends; should it not be, its content is written in the same way, rather than lost or attributed to the next test case, and the run continues.

briefdescription.para: Outputs the prefix for a failing condition.

detaileddescription.para: Called by fail() before the expression text; the prefix includes the message, if any, and the source location.

parameterdescription.para: The message to display.
Whether the failure is associated with an expression.
The source location of the failure.
The test case that owns this check.

briefdescription.para: Outputs the suffix for a failing condition.

detaileddescription.para: Called by fail() after the expression text, to complete the output. The kind of the check lets a reporter show that a failed requirement stops the test case, or aborts the test execution.

parameterdescription.para: The source location of the failure.
The kind of the check (expectation or requirement).
The test case that owns this check.

briefdescription.para: Outputs the prefix for a passing condition.

detaileddescription.para: Called by pass() before the expression text; the prefix includes the message, if any.

parameterdescription.para: The message to display.
The test case that owns this check.

briefdescription.para: Outputs the suffix for a passing condition.

detaileddescription.para: Called by pass() after the expression text, to complete the line.

parameterdescription.para: The test case that owns this check.

briefdescription.para: Writes the current buffered content to the output file.

detaileddescription.para: The buffer is written without appending a line ending, and is not cleared. ANSI colour sequences are removed, so the file receives plain text even when the console output is coloured. If no output file is open, the call has no effect.

Parameters
None.
Returns
Nothing.
Writes the contents of buffer_ to output_file_ without appending a newline. If output_file_ is null, the call is a no-op.
The buffer may contain ANSI colour sequences, added when the console is a terminal, which must not reach the file; they are removed by write_without_colours().

briefdescription.para: Writes formatted text to the console.

detaileddescription.para: All reporter console output is routed through this function, so that it reaches the standard output stream via a single path, shared with the output of the user printf() calls. Using one stream-based path keeps the reporter and user output in the same buffer, preserving their relative order.

format
A printf()-style format string.
...
The arguments referred to by the format string.
Returns
Nothing.
The arguments are forwarded to vfprintf() on stdout. The stream is explicit, so the compiler does not rewrite the call into puts() or putchar(), and all console output shares the same FILE-based path.

briefdescription.para: Writes formatted text to the output file.

detaileddescription.para: If no output file is open, the call has no effect, so callers do not need to check output_file_ themselves.

format
A printf()-style format string.
...
The arguments referred to by the format string.
Returns
Nothing.
The arguments are forwarded to vfprintf() on output_file_. If output_file_ is null, the arguments are ignored.

briefdescription.para: Writes the informational (non-result) lines to the console and to the output file.

detaileddescription.para:
Parameters
None.
Returns
Nothing.
Constructs and emits two informational lines, each prefixed by comment_prefix(): the first lists the program name (without the path) and any command-line arguments; the second identifies the compiler (Clang, GCC, or MSVC) together with the version string, floating-point availability on bare-metal targets, exception support, and any active debug or trace macros. Both lines are written to the output file when one is open, and to stdout when the verbosity is normal or verbose, except when both MICRO_OS_PLUS_STARTUP_ENABLED and MICRO_OS_PLUS_DIAG_TRACE_ENABLED are defined, since the startup code already displays this information.

briefdescription.para: Writes formatted lines to the output file and, when requested, to the console.

detaileddescription.para: The text is formatted once, and the same text is written to the output file, if open, and, when to_console is true, to stdout. As in write_buffer_to_file(), the ANSI colour sequences are removed from the file copy, so a console line with colours and its plain file line are written by one call. The format normally ends with a line ending; any empty line or buffered output that precedes the console line is written by the caller, before this call.

to_console
Whether to write the text to stdout as well.
format
A printf()-style format string.
...
The arguments referred to by the format string.
Returns
Nothing.
The text is formatted with vsnprintf() into a local array, which holds the usual lines without an allocation; a longer text, for example with a long test name, is formatted again, from a copy of the arguments, into a string of the exact length. The array is kept small, since the lines that end the nested test cases are written at the deepest point of the stack. The text is then written with its length to the output file, without the colour sequences (see write_without_colours()), and, when requested, to stdout, unchanged. When there is nowhere to write, or the formatting fails, nothing is written.

briefdescription.para: Formats the elapsed time of a suite or of the session.

detaileddescription.para: The text is appended to the summary lines by the concrete reporters, in the form ", time: 1.234 ms"; it is empty when the stopwatch has no elapsed time, so that the summary lines remain identical on the platforms without a clock.
The array has a fixed size, known at compile time, so that the compiler can verify that the text is never truncated.

stopwatch
The stopwatch of the suite or of the runner.
message
The character array that receives the null-terminated text.
Returns
Nothing.
The elapsed time, in microseconds, is displayed in milliseconds, with three decimals. When it is zero, either because the stopwatch has no readings or because the interval was shorter than a microsecond, the text is empty.

briefdescription.para: Formats the totals of the test session.

detaileddescription.para: The text is the part of the session summary line common to the concrete reporters, in the form "7 checks passed, 1 failed, in 3 test cases, 2 test suites"; the numbers of test cases and of suites skipped by the filter follow the respective counts, as ", 1 skipped", only when not zero. The label (Total: or total:), the markers, and the elapsed time are added by the callers.

runner
The runner of the test session.
message
The character array that receives the null-terminated text.
Returns
Nothing.
The suites are counted by runner::total_suites_count(), which includes the suites skipped by the filter, counted separately by runner::skipped_suites_count().

briefdescription.para: Formats the totals of a suite.

detaileddescription.para: The text is the part of the suite result line common to the concrete reporters: "7 checks in 3 test cases" for a passed suite, and "6 checks passed, 1 failed, in 3 test cases" for a failed one; the number of test cases skipped by the filter follows, as ", 1 skipped", only when not zero. The status, the enclosing markers, and the elapsed time are added by the callers.

suite
The suite that ended.
message
The character array that receives the null-terminated text.
Returns
Nothing.
A passed suite has no failed checks, so only the number of checks is shown.

briefdescription.para: Formats the totals of a test case.

detaileddescription.para: The text is the part of the test case result line common to the concrete reporters: "7 checks" for a passed test case, and "6 checks passed, 1 failed" for a failed one, followed by the number of failed nested test cases, as ", 1 test case failed", only when not zero, since a test case may fail because of a nested one alone. The status and the enclosing markers are added by the callers.

test_case
The test case that ended.
message
The character array that receives the null-terminated text.
Returns
Nothing.
A passed test case has no failed checks and no failed nested test cases, so only the number of checks is shown.

briefdescription.para: Abstract base class for the reporters that display test results, including operand values for failures.

detaileddescription.para: The reporter class is responsible for presenting test results within the µTest++ framework. It accumulates output in a buffer, using basic output operators for strings, characters, booleans, numbers, and pointers, and writes it to the console and to an optional output file.

For failed checks, the reporter prints the actual values of the operands, pre-formatted by its expression_formatter (with type suffixes for numbers). The class supports multiple verbosity levels and colour-coded output to distinguish between passed and failed checks.

The pure virtual member functions report the beginning and end of the session, the suites, and the test cases, and format the pass and fail results; they are implemented by reporter_human and reporter_tap. The concrete reporter is created by the runner, as selected by the --reporter command-line option, or by runner_options::selected_reporter.

The reporters are internal to the framework: their public members are the protocol between the runner, the test nodes, the checks, and the reporter, and custom reporters are not supported. The applications select a reporter with the --reporter command-line option, or with the runner_options, and read the verbosity with runner::verbosity_level().
